entities.name: Sextus Vettulenus Cerialis
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Sextus Vettulenus Cerialis was a Roman senator and military commander, serving as the 1st legate of Judaea from 48 to 52 AD. He was an early supporter of Vespasian, who appointed Cerialis suffect consul in either 72 or 73, during a time of great turmoil in the Roman Empire.


Cerialis played a key role in maintaining order in the province of Judaea, which was crucial for the Roman Empire's stability and prosperity. His leadership and diplomatic skills helped to prevent further instability and ensured the continuation of Roman rule in the region.


Despite his significant contributions to the Roman Empire, Cerialis's legacy has been somewhat overshadowed by the more prominent figures of the time, such as Vespasian and his son Titus. However, his dedication to the Roman Empire and his commitment to maintaining order in Judaea remain an important part of Roman history.


As a testament to his enduring legacy, the Roman province of Cerialis was named in his honor, a lasting tribute to his service and dedication.
